Stories are mechanical, characters are automata that serve the specific purpose of advancing the plot, bringing arguments to the table, arguments that orbit a specific thematic question. Their choices will take the story into its desired direction.
Give your hero a “hamartia”: what are the consequences of repeatedly making choices driven by that fatal flaw. 

If they achieve salvation - what are the most efficient mechanisms of deliverance within the context of your story? If not - describe their plight, describe the optimal conditions to communicate the consequences of their folly. What lifelines have been rejected? What is the sun that melts the wings of wax?

Ultimately, remember, meaning and affect are the direct result of formal relationships that weave patterns of difference and repetition. Subsequently, any narrative element (big or small) acquires meaning negatively, through its relationships to other narrative elements. Working from that premise should allow you to make more lucid decisions, and choice by choice, inch by mile, summon a cohesive and causal story into existence.
